title: What if blood pressure is too low? (top number 90 or less)
v_trigger: Monitor shows 86/52; patient pale, sweaty, dizzy.
v_meaning: Shock: from infection (sepsis), bleeding (e.g. ectopic, blood thinner), severe allergy, dehydration, heart problem, or a medicine (opioid, BP tablet). Or a faulty reading.
v_check_next: Repeat manually/right cuff; look at the patient; heart rate (fast?); temperature; any recent medicine (rash/wheeze?); pregnancy test; Hb; lactate; tummy (rigid?).
v_correct: Call for help; lie flat; assess airway/breathing and start oxygen per protocol to the patient's target; two drips; request a fluid bolus (e.g. 500 mL crystalloid, NICE CG174; the clinician decides volume) and re-check EDUCATIONAL EXAMPLE DOSE (SOURCE-BACKED) — NOT A TRAINEE PRESCRIPTION ; treat cause (antibiotics if septic; adrenaline if anaphylaxis; blood if bleeding).
v_incorrect: Giving a BP tablet or opioid; sending to scan unmonitored; waiting for the next routine obs
v_missed: Progresses to shock: HR rises, confusion, urine stops; lactate rises
v_escalation: Senior surgeon + anaesthetist immediately; gynaecology if pregnancy positive; critical care if not responding.
v_expected_response: After fluid bolus SBP rises above 100 and HR falls within minutes if hypovolaemic; septic shock may need vasopressors
v_next: If BP rises with fluid → continue resuscitation and plan source control. If not → medicines to support BP and intensive care (clinician-controlled). S1: planned operation cancelled; emergency management. S2: resuscitate then urgent surgery if the appendix is the cause.
v_source: RCP NEWS2; Sepsis-3; SSC 2021; NICE NG253
v_validation: Alarm thresholds CONTEXT-DEPENDENT — INSTITUTIONAL PROTOCOL / CLINICIAN CONFIRMATION

title: What if blood pressure is extremely high? (180/110 or more)
v_meaning: Untreated/poorly treated high BP, pain, anxiety, missed tablets; rarely a hypertensive emergency.
v_check_next: Repeat after 5 minutes' rest with correct technique; ask about headache, chest pain, breathlessness, vision, weakness; check usual tablets taken.
v_correct: No symptoms: S1 → postpone and refer for control (don't rush BP down). With symptoms → emergency medical review.
v_incorrect: Rapidly lowering BP on the morning of planned surgery; cancelling after one unrepeated reading
v_missed: Rare: stroke/heart event; more commonly an avoidable cancellation
v_expected_response: Repeat readings often lower after rest; patient rebooked
v_next: S1 rebooked once BP controlled below 160/100 by GP. S2: treat pain, tell anaesthetist; emergency surgery not delayed for BP alone unless organ damage.

title: What if the heart rate is very high? (above 130)
v_meaning: Sepsis, bleeding, dehydration, severe pain, fast abnormal rhythm (AF/SVT), lung clot, fever, thyroid.
v_check_next: Feel pulse: regular or irregular; ECG; BP; temperature; breathing/oxygen; Hb; lactate; pain score.
v_correct: ABCDE; treat cause (pain relief, fluids, antibiotics); ECG-guided rhythm treatment by senior/medical team.
v_incorrect: Treating the number with a rate-slowing drug before finding the cause (e.g. hypovolaemia)
v_escalation: Senior + anaesthetist (NEWS2 3 for this alone = urgent).
v_expected_response: HR falls with analgesia/fluids if pain/dehydration; persists if sepsis/AF
v_next: Settles → continue. Persistent → investigate further; S1 usually deferred after review.

title: What if the heart rate is very slow? (40 or below)
v_meaning: Heart block, beta-blocker/digoxin, very high potassium, hypothermia.
v_check_next: ECG; potassium; medicines; BP; consciousness.
v_correct: ABCDE; stop causative drugs; emergency medicines/pacing per resuscitation team.
v_incorrect: Giving more beta-blocker/opioid; proceeding to anaesthesia
v_expected_response: Improves when cause removed; pacing if heart block
v_next: S1 usually deferred (senior/anaesthetist decide); S2 surgery only once rhythm managed.

title: What if the patient has a fever? (38.0 °C or more)
v_meaning: S1: inflamed gallbladder or infected bile ducts (if jaundiced); urine/chest infection. S2: appendicitis, worse if 39+ (possible perforation/abscess).
v_check_next: Heart rate, BP, breathing (sepsis?); tummy exam (Murphy's / generalised tenderness); jaundice; urine dipstick; chest; WBC/CRP; blood cultures if 38.5+ or rigors; lactate.
v_correct: Paracetamol; fluids if dry; antibiotics according to cause; sepsis bundle if criteria met.
v_incorrect: S1: proceeding with the planned operation; treating fever only with paracetamol without looking for a source
v_escalation: Senior (in S1 the pathway changes, so yes).
v_expected_response: Temperature falls with paracetamol but source signs remain → pathway changes
v_next: S1: removed from planned list → acute pathway. S2: continue towards surgery; if complicated, faster.

title: What if the patient is cold? (36.0 °C or less)
v_meaning: Cold environment, long fasting, older age — or severe sepsis (ominous if with other bad signs).
v_check_next: Other vital signs; sepsis screen if unwell.
v_correct: Warm (forced-air blanket); don't send to theatre until 36.0 unless urgent CLINICAL REFERENCE — SOURCE BACKED (NICE CG65).
v_incorrect: Transferring a cold patient for planned surgery
v_missed: More bleeding and wound infection; shivering
v_expected_response: Warms ~0.5–1 °C per hour with forced air CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
v_next: Warmed → continue.

title: What if oxygen saturation is low? (below 94%)
v_meaning: Probe error; aspiration (vomit in lungs); chest infection; fluid overload after many boluses; lung clot; too much opioid (slow breathing); collapsed lung areas from pain.
v_check_next: Check probe and wave; look at patient (colour, effort); breathing rate; listen to chest; fluid balance; opioids given; blood gas; chest X-ray.
v_correct: Look at the patient and assess airway/breathing; check probe and waveform; if the low reading is real, sit up and start oxygen per protocol to the patient's target range (94–98%, or 88–92% if at risk of hypercapnic failure); find the cause (stop fluids if overloaded per senior; stimulate if over-sedated — antidote by clinician); reassess within minutes (process in Part 4.5).
v_incorrect: Ignoring because 'probe is wrong' without checking; high-flow O2 to a CO2 retainer without monitoring
v_escalation: Anaesthetist/senior urgently; emergency team if 88% or below.
v_expected_response: SpO2 returns to target with appropriate oxygen within minutes if cause treatable
v_next: Improves with modest oxygen → continue, anaesthetist informed. Worsens → airway team; case may stop.

title: What if breathing is very fast? (25 or more)
v_meaning: Sepsis, acid build-up (DKA, poor circulation), lung problem, pain, anxiety.
v_check_next: Oxygen, temperature, BP, blood gas (acid), lactate, sugar/ketones, chest exam.
v_correct: Treat cause; sepsis bundle if infection.
v_incorrect: Giving a sedative to 'calm' the patient
v_expected_response: RR falls as cause treated
v_next: Re-assess every 15–30 min.

title: What if breathing is very slow? (8 or less)

v_expected_response: RR and alertness improve after stimulation/antidote
v_next: Recovers → review pain plan.

title: What if the patient becomes confused?
v_meaning: Low sugar, low oxygen, sepsis, low BP, opioids, low sodium, alcohol withdrawal, stroke.
v_check_next: Finger-prick sugar FIRST, oxygen, BP, temperature, drug chart, sodium, face/arm weakness.
v_correct: Treat what's found (sugar below 4 → glucose); sepsis bundle if infection; reassess capacity (consent may be invalid now).
v_incorrect: Assuming it is 'just pain medicine' without checking glucose
v_escalation: Senior urgently (NEWS2 3); medical team if stroke signs.
v_expected_response: Rapid improvement after glucose if hypoglycaemic
v_next: Recovered → re-confirm consent.

title: What if pain gets much worse or the tummy becomes rigid?
v_trigger: Pain 9/10 despite strong painkiller; whole tummy hard as a board.
v_meaning: Perforation (burst appendix/gallbladder), ruptured ectopic, twisted ovary, blocked/ischaemic bowel.
v_check_next: Re-examine; vital signs; lactate; pregnancy test; Hb; imaging.
v_correct: Pain relief; nil by mouth; fluids; antibiotics; prepare for urgent surgery.
v_incorrect: Giving more analgesia without re-examining or calling the senior
v_expected_response: Pain may ease with analgesia but rigidity persists
v_next: Surgery expedited.

title: What if potassium is high? (above 5.3)
v_meaning: Faulty (haemolysed) sample; kidney injury; medicines (ACE inhibitors, potassium-sparing water tablets, potassium supplements); acid in blood.
v_check_next: Lab comment; ECG (peaked T waves?); creatinine; medicines; repeat.
v_correct: 5.5–5.9 (mild, UKKA): ECG, repeat, review drugs. 6.0–6.4: urgent repeat + ECG, treat if real. 6.5+ or ECG changes: emergency treatment (calcium to protect the heart; insulin-glucose) PATIENT-SPECIFIC DOSE — CLINICIAN CONTROLLED ; heart monitor.
v_incorrect: Emergency treatment of an obviously haemolysed sample with normal ECG; ignoring a real 6.5+
v_escalation: Senior + anaesthetist (6.0+); emergency team if ECG changes.
v_expected_response: K falls ~0.6–1.0 mmol/L after insulin–glucose (UKKA) — repeat level
v_next: S1 usually deferred (senior/anaesthetist decide) until normal; S2 corrected before/at anaesthesia.
v_validation: Treatment doses PATIENT-SPECIFIC DOSE — CLINICIAN CONTROLLED

title: What if potassium is low? (below 3.5)
v_meaning: Vomiting, diarrhoea, water tablets.
v_check_next: ECG (flat T, U waves); magnesium; ongoing losses.

v_incorrect: Fast undiluted IV potassium (dangerous); not checking magnesium
v_expected_response: K rises on repeat after replacement
v_next: S1 usually deferred after review if below 3.0 CLINICAL INTERPRETATION ; S2 correct during resuscitation, proceed when safe.
v_source: Typical bands (no single guideline); hospital potassium protocol
v_validation: Replacement protocol CONTEXT-DEPENDENT — INSTITUTIONAL PROTOCOL / CLINICIAN CONFIRMATION

title: What if sodium is abnormal?
v_meaning: Water tablets, vomiting replaced by plain water, hormonal causes, heart/liver failure.
v_check_next: Alertness (confusion?), fluid status, medicines, repeat.
v_correct: Correct the cause slowly (no faster than ~8–10 mmol/L per day).
v_incorrect: Rapid correction (risk of osmotic demyelination)
v_escalation: Senior + anaesthetist; medical team if below 125.
v_expected_response: Slow change on repeat (≤10 mmol/L first 24 h)
v_next: S1 usually deferred after review if below 130 or above 150 CLINICAL INTERPRETATION ; S2 correct in parallel.

title: What if haemoglobin is low?
v_meaning: Long-term iron deficiency, thalassaemia trait, slow gut bleeding, or acute bleeding (S2 ectopic).
v_check_next: Previous Hb; red cell size (MCV); vital signs (bleeding now?); pregnancy test; stool history.
v_correct: S1: investigate before planned surgery; S2: group & save/crossmatch, look for bleeding, transfusion decision if below 70 (80 heart disease).
v_incorrect: Proceeding with planned surgery without investigating unexplained anaemia; transfusing a stable patient above threshold
v_expected_response: Hb rises ~10 g/L per unit transfused CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
v_next: S1 usually postponed for investigation CONTEXT-DEPENDENT — INSTITUTIONAL PROTOCOL / CLINICIAN CONFIRMATION ; S2 proceeds with blood available.
v_validation: Postponement rule CONTEXT-DEPENDENT — INSTITUTIONAL PROTOCOL / CLINICIAN CONFIRMATION

title: What if the white cell count is high?
v_meaning: Infection/inflammation (appendicitis, gallbladder), steroids, stress, pregnancy.
v_check_next: Temperature, heart rate, exam, CRP, score.
v_correct: Interpret in context; S1 high WBC = not routine → acute pathway; S2 supports diagnosis; above 18 = moderate gallbladder grade.
v_incorrect: Treating the number alone; ignoring it in a planned patient
v_escalation: Senior if S1 or if very high.
v_expected_response: Falls with treatment over days
v_next: Pathway decided by the whole picture.

title: What if the white cell count is low?
v_meaning: Overwhelming sepsis, viral illness, medicines, bone-marrow problem.
v_check_next: Neutrophils (below 0.5 = critical); vital signs; sepsis screen.
v_correct: Treat as serious if infection present; urgent antibiotics if septic.
